criteria.quote: Kangaskhan sleeps standing, or risks crushing its baby.
criteria.revision: Delay the answer and open with: "Its infant can stay in the pouch until three years old—but how does Kangaskhan sleep without crushing it?"

criteria.quote: Its baby is carried in a pouch on its belly.
criteria.revision: Replace the generic claim "Its strangest sleeping posture is really a protective design" with the concrete Pokédex explanation: "It sleeps standing up to avoid crushing the baby in its pouch."

criteria.quote: Can Kangaskhan protect its baby without lying down?
criteria.revision: Make the question genuinely unresolved before the reveal: "The baby may stay in the pouch for roughly three years—but what happens when Kangaskhan sleeps?"

criteria.quote: So Kangaskhan always sleeps standing up to avoid crushing the baby.
criteria.revision: Replace the repeated sleep explanation in the middle with a new sourced escalation: "The baby only leaves when it feels safe—and the adult keeps a close eye on it." Then reveal the standing-sleep fact afterward.

Move the standing-sleep reveal out of the title and first scene. Build first with "The infant rarely leaves its mother's pouch until three years old," then reveal: "To avoid crushing it, Kangaskhan always sleeps standing up."

Replace "A POSTURE WITH PURPOSE" and its caption with a distinct sourced detail: "When the child finally leaves home after roughly three years, that is the only time the mother is heard to cry wildly."

criteria.quote: Standing keeps the infant's protective pouch from being crushed during sleep.
criteria.revision: Make the ending synthesize the duration and the posture: "For an infant that may stay in the pouch for roughly three years, Kangaskhan's sleep is standing-only—the Pokédex says it does this to avoid crushing the baby."

criteria.quote: Best parenting move, or too big a sacrifice?
criteria.revision: Replace the unsupported idea of sacrifice with a sourced comparison: "Which proves its protection more: sleeping standing to avoid crushing the baby, or never giving up in battle to protect it?"

findings.quote: So Kangaskhan always sleeps standing up to avoid crushing the baby.
findings.note: Scene "sleeping-safely" repeats scene "standing-or-crushed". Replace it with a new step in the story.
